import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
        df = df.astype({
            'admit': 'int64',
            'gre': 'int64',
            'gpa': 'float64',
            'prestige': 'int64'
        })
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Since all sources have the same schema and represent similar data,
    # the transformation is essentially union all rows.

    # Optional: If duplicates should be removed, uncomment the next line
    # combined_df = combined_df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

    # Final check: ensure columns are in the target schema order
    combined_df = combined_df[['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']]

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    combined_df.to_csv(
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_66/target_multisource_cot.csv",
        index=False
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
